requirements.text: Create a problem record to capture this newly identified issue with the expired Adobe enterprise license ... For this software problem, set impact and urgency to their maximum available levels
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_003' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%enterprise%' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%adobe%' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%license%' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%expired%' AND status = 'new' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND category = 'software'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (PRB_003 after PRB_002); the request creates one problem
impact = high and urgency = high are the maximum levels in policy 9's enumerations; priority = critical follows from policy 4.2's matrix (high x high)
status = new is policy 4.2's default for a new problem
category = software from the request's words 'this software problem'

the problem_statement predicates are the request's own words for the cause (expired enterprise Adobe license); SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII, so the cells equal the benchmark's LOWER() form
opened_by, short_description and original_task are not fixed by the request and not tested by the benchmark; not tested

requirements.text: this problem needs to be associate it with the previous incident so that this situation is properly recorded
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_005' AND problem = 'PRB_003'
assumptions: the incident assigned to Carlos (USER_003) about a software installation is INC_005 'Software installation request' (description 'Request for Adobe Creative Suite installation', category software); his other four incidents are email, printer, monitor and keyboard, so the match is unique
the association is recorded in incident.problem, as the benchmark check tests it; problem.original_task is not tested
the incident's own impact/urgency are not tested: 'now considered a major incident' describes the situation and the request fixes maximum levels for the problem only
the policy's 'incident_to_problem related list' has no table in this schema; the link is the incident.problem column, as the benchmark checks

requirements.text: Send a report to the user who reported this incident with the subject Urgent Update: Licensing Issue Affecting Your Software Installation. In the message, greet the reporter by their full name and apologize clearly ...

cells.subject: Urgent Update: Licensing Issue Affecting Your Software Installation

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_005' AND email = 'aisha.williams@techcorp.com' AND type = 'report' AND subject = 'Urgent Update: Licensing Issue Affecting Your Software Installation' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%aisha williams%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%apolog%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%highly urgent problem%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%enterprise%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%adobe%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%license%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%expired%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%longer%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%address%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%recommend%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%focus%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%performance%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%daily%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%block%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008); the request sends one notification
the user who reported INC_005 is its caller_id USER_004 (Aisha Williams, aisha.williams@techcorp.com, active) on the seed; the incident table has no opened_by column
type = report from the request's word 'report'; subject quoted exactly from the request

every message predicate is a word or phrase of the request (full name, apology, highly urgent problem, what the problem is about, longer, addressed, recommend, focus, daily performance, blocking), as the benchmark check tests them; SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII
status not fixed by request or policy and not tested by the benchmark; not tested

requirements.text: this problem needs to be associate it with the previous incident (no other incident is linked)
requirements.selector: incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND problem IS NOT NULL
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND problem IS NOT NULL
assumptions: boundary of the incident description: Carlos's four other incidents (email, printer, monitor, keyboard) and the other software incidents must not be linked to a problem; no incident carries a problem on the seed

disagreement: selector: A incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND problem = 'PRB_003', B assigned_to = 'USER_003' AND incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND problem IS NOT NULL; chose incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND problem IS NOT NULL because it implies both (the task creates one problem and links one incident, so any other incident gaining any problem is outside the request)

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the three benchmark checks (all kept), the problem (PRB_003: high impact and urgency, critical priority, status new, category software, the request's words in problem_statement), the link on INC_005's problem column and the report notification (NOTIF_008 to the caller USER_004 Aisha Williams).
disagreement: stay that no other incident is linked to the problem: A selects any incident other than INC_005 with problem = 'PRB_003', B selects Carlos's other incidents with any problem; chose any incident other than INC_005 with any problem, which implies both (logged on the requirement).
Both passes read 'which is now considered a major incident because it is affecting the whole company' as describing the situation (the policy 4.2 trigger for a problem), not as an instruction to change INC_005's impact or urgency: the request's only 'set impact and urgency' instruction is 'for this software problem'; an agent that also raises them is a collateral change measured separately. The policy's knowledge-search rule applies to incident creation, not problem creation, so no incident_knowledge requirement is written. The problem's opened_by and original_task are untested since nothing fixes them. Acting user USER_001 (Marcus Thompson) is admin, so creating the problem and updating the incident are within scope.
